articles.title: 中国民政部：争取十五五末建成县乡村三级养老服务网络

articles.author: Bloomberg
articles.description:
Singapore said it ran a trade deficit with the US in 2024, disputing figures published by Washington that showed the city state posted a surplus and challenging suggestions that it is contributing to global manufacturing overcapacity.
The dispute surfaced after the Office of the US Trade Representative announced this week that it had launched investigations under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974 into the acts, policies and practices of 16 economies, including Singapore. The investigations...
articles.title: Singapore contests US claim of trade surplus amid excess capacity probe

articles.author: Xinmei Shen
articles.description:
US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth said on Friday that Iran’s new Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei has been injured and pledged to continue ramping up attacks, while playing down the impact of the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz.
Khamenei is “wounded and likely disfigured”, Hegseth said during a press conference on Friday morning. The new Iranian leader’s first public address, issued on Thursday through a written statement, showed that “he’s scared, he’s injured, he’s on the run, and he...
articles.title: US says Iran’s new supreme leader likely ‘wounded’, dismisses Strait of Hormuz concerns

articles.author: Reuters
articles.description:
Long before the US and Israel ⁠attacked Iran, the Islamic Republic had devised its own weapon: holding the world’s main ⁠oil lifeline hostage to offset its foes’ military superiority, three regional sources familiar with Iranian planning said.
For decades, Iran has signalled that if pushed into a confrontation, it would restrict tanker traffic in the Strait of Hormuz, the chokepoint where its adversaries are most exposed because disruptions there reverberate instantly through global energy...
articles.title: How Iran turned Strait of Hormuz into potent weapon against US bombardment

articles.author: Xiaofei Xu
articles.description:
Trade talks between China and the United States in Paris this weekend are likely to focus on setting the scene for the Beijing summit between President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump later this month, analysts said, downplaying the prospects of any significant breakthroughs.
Vice-Premier He Lifeng and US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent are expected to discuss potential deals on tariffs, investment, and trade in soybeans and rare earths, which would be presented as deliverables for the...
articles.title: US-China trade talks: what to expect as senior officials meet in Paris

articles.author: Agence France-Presse
articles.description:
The US economy grew at a significantly slower pace than initially estimated for the final months of 2025, government data showed on Friday, a major downgrade that comes as fallout from war in the Middle East looms.
US gross domestic product rose at an annual rate of 0.7 per cent in the fourth quarter, the Commerce Department said.
This was sharply down from its earlier estimated 1.4 per cent over the October to December period.
It also indicates that the world’s biggest economy was on a weaker...
articles.title: US economic growth slumps to 0.7% in fourth quarter, stoking inflation worries

articles.author: Agence France-Presse,Associated Press
articles.description:
In-form Alanna Kennedy and skipper Sam Kerr produced spectacular strikes as Australia overcame a talented North Korea 2-1 to reach the semi-finals of the Women’s Asian Cup on Friday.
Kicking off the knockout phase, the Matildas were outplayed by their youthful opponents for large chunks of a tense match in front of 16,466 fans at Perth Rectangular Stadium.
But they took their chances with Kennedy firing her fifth tournament goal with a left-foot bullet from the edge of the box in the ninth...
articles.title: Australia edge North Korea to reach Women’s Asian Cup semi-finals, clinch World Cup berth

articles.author: Wency Chen,Ben Jiang
articles.description:
The OpenClaw craze is rapidly driving up prices and depleting stock of Apple’s Mac Mini compact computer across China, according to local sellers, as consumers scramble to secure machines capable of safely running the open-source artificial intelligence agent amid a nationwide rush to “raise a lobster”.
Beijing electronics seller Frank Chai said he was asking for a mark-up of at least 500 yuan (US$73) for a basic Mac Mini model, which comes with 16 gigabytes (GB) of memory and 256GB storage and...
articles.title: Apple’s Mac Mini selling out across China as OpenClaw fever rages

articles.author: Victoria Bela
articles.description:
The use of artificial intelligence (AI) in the US-Israel war on Iran has sparked a legal and ethical debate, as well as condemnation from countries including China after a deadly missile strike on a primary school.
To prepare for its operations against Iran, the US military reportedly used Palantir’s Maven Smart System, an AI platform that incorporates models like Anthropic’s Claude to aggregate large amounts of data.
A US-based source familiar with the matter said the only thing that Claude or...
articles.title: Deadly strike on Iranian primary school raises questions about AI, accountability

articles.author: Lam Ka-sing
articles.description:
More than 400 foreign domestic helpers gathered at an international school campus in Hong Kong on Friday as 50 students paid tribute to their contributions as “second mothers” who help shape a multicultural environment at home.
The organising student committee for the event at the English Schools Foundation’s Renaissance College in Ma On Shan said it hoped to inspire the wider community to cherish their domestic workers.
The “Jie Jie Day” event, held annually by the school for 14 years, was also...
articles.title: Hong Kong students honour over 400 foreign domestic helpers as ‘second mothers’

articles.author: Kevin Li
articles.description:
Hong Kong authorities have asked all government units not to install OpenClaw or its variants due to security concerns, days after some mainland Chinese entities were reported to have restricted the use of the AI agent.
The government’s Digital Policy Office (DPO) told the South China Morning Post on Friday that while no related security incidents had been reported, it noted the potential risks of the use of the artificial intelligence agent, including unauthorised data access, leakage and...
articles.title: Hong Kong government workers warned not to install OpenClaw due to security risks

articles.author: Ambrose Li,William Yiu
articles.description:
Hong Kong’s physiotherapy sector has urged the government to expand employment opportunities for locally trained professionals, warning that severe funding cuts will lead to a glut of practitioners, with the surplus projected to exceed 2,000 by 2040.
In a letter to the authorities, the Hong Kong Physiotherapy Association pointed to hiring freezes and job losses at NGOs as a result of budget cuts, even as the government continued to subsidise the training of physiotherapists.
“These developments...
articles.title: Funding cuts trigger calls for help on jobs from Hong Kong’s physiotherapists

articles.author: Laura Zhou
articles.description:
China and Vietnam are to hold their first high-level ministerial talks under a new platform next week.
This comes as the neighbours seek to cement their strategic alignment despite heightened tensions over Beijing’s purported new land reclamation work in the disputed South China Sea.
According to the Chinese foreign ministry, Foreign Minister Wang Yi, Public Security Minister Wang Xiaohong and Defence Minister Dong Jun will be in Vietnam from Sunday to Tuesday to meet their respective...
articles.title: Will Paracels dispute overshadow China and Vietnam’s drive for stronger strategic ties?

articles.author: Fiona Sun
articles.description:
Twenty-one people have been injured in a crash involving two double-decker buses, a truck and a car on Yuen Long Highway in Hong Kong.
Police said on Friday that the force was alerted to the traffic accident at 6.35pm.
As of 8pm, 12 women and nine men had suffered minor injuries, police said. Among them was the driver of the private car, the force added.

Franchised bus firm KMB said two double-deckers on routes 276B and 269B were involved in the accident with the two other vehicles while...
articles.title: 21 hurt in 4-vehicle crash on Hong Kong’s Yuen Long Highway

articles.author: Xinyi Wu,Carol Yang
articles.description:
Ships near the Strait of Hormuz are broadcasting Chinese affiliations in an apparent bid to avoid attack, at a time when Iran’s new supreme leader vows to keep the strategic waterway closed.
The crews of at least 11 vessels sitting in the Gulf of Oman and the Persian Gulf had their transponders set to announce Chinese links on Friday afternoon, according to Kpler’s MarineTraffic data platform.
The broadcasts were a defensive measure, said Cui Shoujun, director of the Institute of International...
articles.title: Strait of Hormuz transiting ships flash ‘China owner’ signals to evade Iran blockade

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
Cuban President Miguel Diaz-Canel said on Friday that his government has held recent talks with the US, marking the first time the Caribbean country confirms such speculation.
He said the talks “were aimed at finding solutions through dialogue to the bilateral differences between our two nations. International factors facilitated these exchanges”.
He did not elaborate on those factors.
Diaz-Canel said no petroleum shipments have arrived on the island in the past three months, which he blamed on...
articles.title: Cuba confirms talks with US as island gasps under Trump’s energy blockade

articles.author: Andrew Sheng
articles.description:
The US-Israeli attacks on Iran have profound implications for the global governance order. For America, the world’s mightiest power, to attack another nation without congressional or UN approval condemns the rules-based order to the dustbin of history.
Governance is about checks and balance by rules, self-restraint or simply a humble appreciation that waging “forever wars” often ends up in self-destruction. War is such an extreme and costly measure it should only be undertaken after careful...
articles.title: US-Israeli war on Iran makes a mockery of global governance rules

articles.author: Biman Mukherji
articles.description:
India’s Supreme Court has allowed the parents of a 31-year-old man to withdraw life-sustaining treatment after more than a decade in a vegetative state, a ruling experts say could shape how the country implements its legal framework for passive euthanasia.
The decision in the case of Harish Rana is widely seen as one of the clearest real-world applications of the principle that patients have a right to die with dignity under India’s constitution.
Rana, an engineering student, had been in a...
articles.title: Indian man in 13-year vegetative state allowed to die by Supreme Court

articles.author: Shi Huang
articles.description:
In the high-stakes race for radar supremacy, China could leap two generations ahead of the United States following an advancement in semiconductor technology published last month that is poised to redefine the future of military electronics.
While the US Air Force struggles to modernise its fighter fleet with gallium nitride-based radar systems, Chinese engineers are already pioneering the next frontier: gallium oxide semiconductors with built-in data storage capabilities.
Today’s Chinese...
articles.title: Could China’s gallium oxide leap leave US F-22 radar 2 generations behind?

articles.author: Cao Jiaxuan
articles.description:
Beijing on Friday warned Washington against making moves involving Hong Kong or Taiwan ahead of the coming visit by US President Donald Trump later this month.
It condemned United States’ calls for the release of jailed former Hong Kong media boss Jimmy Lai Chee-ying and reiterated opposition to American arms sales to the self-ruled island.
Speaking at a regular press briefing, Chinese foreign ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun said Lai “should be severely punished according to the law”, and accused...
articles.title: Beijing warns US over Jimmy Lai, Hong Kong and Taiwan arms sales ahead of Trump visit

articles.author: Josh Ball
articles.description:
Bryson DeChambeau opened up a three-shot lead at the halfway stage of LIV Golf Singapore on Friday, and credited a love of “chocolate milk and hitting more drivers” for his success.
The American’s six-under-par 65 at Sentosa Golf Club took him to 10 under for tournament, with five players, including Jon Rahm and Thomas Detry, tied for second.
One of four overnight leaders, DeChambeau said after his first round the unlikely pairing had been key to his preparation for the season and reiterated...
articles.title: LIV Golf Singapore: ‘chocolate milk, drivers’ help give Bryson DeChambeau a 3-shot lead

articles.author: dpa
articles.description:
UK Foreign Secretary Yvette Cooper has accused Russia and Iran of attempting to “hijack the global economy” as Tehran continued to blockade a major oil shipping route.
Iran’s new supreme leader has vowed to continue attacking shipping in the Strait of Hormuz in retaliation for ongoing US-Israeli strikes on his country.
The blockade has seen oil prices jump to around US$100 per barrel, threatening higher inflation across the globe.
Speaking to the media during a visit to Saudi Arabia, the UK...
articles.title: UK says Russia, Iran trying to ‘hijack global economy’ amid Hormuz blockade

articles.author: Joseph Sipalan
articles.description:
The cost of Malaysia’s subsidies for fuel at the pump is projected to rise by more than four times in the short term, the government has said, as it rushed to assure the public the country’s energy supply will not be disrupted even as the Iran war chokes global oil and gas shipments.
Fear of an energy crisis has engulfed much of Southeast Asia since the US and Israel launched air strikes on Iran on February 28, pushing Tehran to close the Strait of Hormuz – a vital waterway that handles about a...
articles.title: Malaysia’s fuel subsidy bill to rise more than fourfold as Iran war drags on

articles.author: Cheryl Arcibal
articles.description:
JPMorgan Chase has committed to leasing about 250,000 sq ft of space in the new Sun Hung Kai Properties (SHKP) office towers in Hong Kong’s West Kowloon district for 10 years, making the US investment bank the anchor tenant of the 700,000 sq ft mixed-use development, the Hong Kong-listed developer said on Friday.
Artist Square Towers (AST) will house the bank’s Kowloon office, which is currently located at The Quayside in Kowloon East, starting in the latter half of 2028, according to an...
articles.title: JPMorgan signs up as anchor tenant for SHKP’s West Kowloon office development

articles.author: Ng Kang-chung
articles.description:
A union representing employees of Hong Kong’s rail operator, the MTR Corporation, has expressed disappointment with the firm’s refusal to consider their calls for improved benefits, saying the pay rise of up to 3.84 per cent for most staff is “slightly below demands”.
The MTR Corp announced pay increases on Friday ranging from 1.6 to 3.84 per cent for most non-management staff for the 2026-27 financial year, depending on their performance. Last year, the adjustment was between 1.8 and 5.4 per...
articles.title: Hong Kong MTR Corp pay rise below expectations: union

articles.author: Reuters
articles.description:
Top names in ⁠Hollywood will gather on March 15 to hand out the ⁠annual Academy Awards at a red-carpet ceremony brimming with drama in the major races.
One Battle After Another, starring Leonardo DiCaprio as a one-time political radical now parenting a teenager, was seen as the front runner for the coveted best picture prize after stacking up trophy after trophy at recent ceremonies.
The vampire story Sinners, a celebration of blues music ‌and black culture in the segregation-era US South, made...
articles.title: Sinners up against One Battle After Another for best picture at the Academy Awards

articles.author: Paul McNamara
articles.description:
Coleman Wong Chak-lam said he had drawn inspiration from superstar pair Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner after he coolly ignored a confrontational outburst from opponent Damir Dzumhur to secure a three-set victory and a spot in the Copa Cap Cana quarter-finals in the Dominican Republic.
The Hongkonger irritated Dzumhur when he clenched his fist in the direction of his support team after the Bosnian double-faulted to hand Wong a 4-1 lead in the deciding set.
As Wong marched to his seat, Dzumhur...
articles.title: Coleman Wong stays cool in face of opponent’s outburst to reach last 8 of Challenger event

articles.author: Luna Sun
articles.description:
Japan’s unilateral decision to release oil from its emergency stockpiles highlights its vulnerability to prolonged supply disruptions and may leave it more exposed to economic pressure from China amid tense bilateral relations, according to analysts.
Tokyo announced earlier this week that it planned to release a total of 80 million barrels starting March 16, marking the first time it would independently tap its national reserves. The decision came ahead of a coordinated response by the...
articles.title: Japan taps oil reserves as Iran war spreads. Could it give China leverage?

articles.author: Ishani Sarkar
articles.description:
John F. Kennedy Jr, son of former US president John F. Kennedy and Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis, is widely considered one of America’s most timeless heartthrobs. The late attorney and publisher is now back in the spotlight thanks to FX’s Love Story. The hit series executive-produced by Ryan Murphy, which focuses on JFK Jr’s whirlwind romance with fashion publicist Carolyn Bessette, is currently the most popular title on Hulu, according to streaming data collection website FlixPatrol.

The success...
articles.title: Who did JFK Jr date before his Love Story with Carolyn Bessette?

articles.author: Dannie Peng
articles.description:
The sudden death of prominent Chinese genetic psychologist Li Xinying while travelling in Egypt has sparked growing concern and speculation in China, as official explanations about the cause remain vague and medically inconclusive.
Li, 48, a researcher and doctoral supervisor at the Chinese Academy of Sciences’ (CAS) Institute of Psychology, died on February 23 at 10pm Beijing time, according to an online obituary.
The stated cause of death was “non-specific respiratory failure”, an obituary...
articles.title: Death of Chinese scientist Li Xinying, 48, in Egypt raises sharp questions back home

articles.author: Fran Lu
articles.description:
More than a million people online have been touched by a Chinese man who posted a huge note on his illiterate mother-in-law’s suitcase to help in case she needed help during her first solo flight.
On February 28, the man from Xian city, northwestern China’s Shaanxi province, posted that his mother-in-law would be flying on the same evening to Dalian, in northeastern China’s Liaoning province.
He said that the woman, who is in her 60s, is illiterate and does not speak Mandarin. The flight also...
articles.title: Chinese man posts a big note on mother-in-law’s suitcase to seek help for her solo travel

articles.author: Resty Woro Yuniar
articles.description:
Powerful waves have chewed away large sections of Bali’s iconic Kuta Beach, raising fresh concern about the future of the Indonesian island’s most famous stretch of sand.
Officials say the latest damage, driven by recent rough seas, has intensified a long-running problem of coastal erosion that experts warn is being worsened by extreme weather and decades of coastal development on the resort island.
Abrasion along Kuta’s shoreline is not new, but officials say this year’s extreme weather has...
articles.title: Is Bali’s Kuta Beach disappearing? Coastal erosion crisis threatens famed shoreline

articles.author: Julie Zhang
articles.description:
In a landmark development, Neuracle Medical Technology has secured the country’s first-ever approval for an implantable brain-computer interface (BCI) system designed to restore hand motor function in patients with spinal cord injuries, in a regulatory milestone that underscores China’s accelerating push in neurotechnology.
China’s BCI start-ups, seen as potential rivals to Elon Musk’s Neuralink, are gaining momentum as regulatory support and fresh capital fuel growth.
Shares of BCI companies...
articles.title: In a first for China, Neuracle’s implantable brain-computer interface wins approval

articles.author: Olivia O'Sullivan
articles.description:
Hong Kong stars Ka Ying Rising and Romantic Warrior have topped the latest edition of the Longines World’s Best Racehorse Rankings, the first time the city has occupied both spots.
The David Hayes-trained Ka Ying Rising headlines the rankings, remaining Hong Kong’s highest-rated racehorse in history on a mark of 128, while the Danny Shum Chap-shing-trained Romantic Warrior was close behind with a rating of 124.
Third place in the list, which was released on Thursday, went to Japanese...
articles.title: Ka Ying Rising tops Longines World’s Best Racehorse Rankings; final Derby field revealed

articles.author: Reuters
articles.description:
Formula 1 championship leader George Russell put Mercedes on pole position for the first sprint race of the season in China on Friday in a front-row lockout with teammate Kimi Antonelli.
Russell led every ‌phase of the session at the Shanghai circuit to take his first career sprint pole in a time of one minute, 31.520 seconds. Antonelli was 0.289 slower.
McLaren’s Lando Norris will start third after the reigning champion told stewards he had not been on a proper “push” ‌lap when Antonelli, who...
articles.title: Formula 1: George Russell puts Mercedes on pole for the Chinese Grand Prix sprint race

articles.author: Alcott Wei
articles.description:
Beijing is using AI to help its radars better detect low-altitude drones, according to a top Chinese military scientist who cited drone swarm tactics in the US’ ongoing attack on Iran as an emerging pressure on radar.
This development was revealed on Wednesday by Xu Jin, a leading air-defence radar expert and a member of China’s top political advisory body, the National Committee of the Chinese People’s Political Consultative Conference (CPPCC).
On the sidelines of Beijing’s “two sessions”...
articles.title: China announces AI boost to radar as drone swarms confound detectors in Iran war

articles.author: David Dodwell
articles.description:
Spare a thought for the iceberg A23a which, after an extraordinary 40-year life voyaging around the southern Atlantic Ocean, is this month expected to die unnoticed close to the island of South Georgia, a mess of “brash ice, small icebergs and bergy bits”.
A23a was one of the largest “megabergs” to be spawned in our lifetimes. When it broke away from the Filchner Ice Shelf into the Weddell Sea in Western Antarctica in 1986, it covered an area of around 4,000 sq km – about the size of Hong Kong...
articles.title: How an iceberg’s ‘final dance’ tells a story about our past and future

articles.author: Iman Muttaqin Yusof
articles.description:
As soaring copper prices make the metal highly sought after, more cable thieves are targeting some of Malaysia’s busiest urban rail lines, causing significant inconvenience to commuters and headaches for authorities aiming to combat the scourge.
Thefts of copper-embedded cables have led to disruption in train services linking Kuala Lumpur’s northern suburbs to the federal administrative capital of Putrajaya in recent weeks.
Among the services affected are the high-speed MRT Putrajaya and Kajang...
articles.title: Cable thefts at key Malaysian train lines soar amid copper’s red-hot demand

articles.author: Agence France-Presse
articles.description:
China coach Ante Milicic urged his players on Friday to remain “calm and confident” in a charged Women’s Asian Cup quarter-final against Chinese Taipei.
The reigning champions are targeting a record-extending 10th continental title but are wary of opponents who have shown improvement as the tournament has progressed.
Chinese Taipei were beaten 2-0 by strongly fancied Japan in the group phase but were by no means outclassed.
“They gave Japan a very difficult game and then went on to win their...
articles.title: Women’s Asian Cup: China coach tells players to stay ‘calm’ in Chinese Taipei quarter-final

articles.author: Morning Studio editors,Jacqueline Kot
articles.description:
Li Xiaopeng is China’s most decorated gymnast, having won 16 world titles, including four Olympic gold medals. Although he retired from the sport in 2009, the mindset and principles he carried as an elite athlete continue to apply to his other roles in life, namely those of a father and an entrepreneur.
Li recently met with Victoria Tang-Owen – a Hong Kong-based designer and creative director as well as a fellow parent – to discuss how being a history-making, successful athlete has influenced...
articles.title: Olympic champion Li Xiaopeng draws from golden legacy to succeed in personal life

articles.author: Vanessa Cai
articles.description:
In January, the US-based magazine Newsweek reported that China had started dredging sand on an obscure feature in the Paracel Islands, the archipelago known as Xisha by the Chinese and Hoang Sa in Vietnam.
More recent satellite images suggest that China has significantly expanded its reclamation, with the once-submerged Antelope Reef appearing to have a substantially larger surface area.
The reef, one of more than 30 islands that make up the Paracels in the South China Sea, is claimed by Beijing...
articles.title: What’s important about Antelope Reef in the South China Sea’s Paracel Islands?

articles.author: Reuters
articles.description:
Vietnam produced the largest trade surplus with the United States in January, overtaking both Mexico and China, latest official US data shows, as its exports rose sharply while Chinese direct shipments to the United States fell.
Hanoi has been negotiating a trade deal with Washington for months but no agreement has been reached because of the large trade gap and disagreements over tariff rates the US wants to impose on Vietnamese goods, officials have said.
In January, Vietnam’s trade surplus...
articles.title: Vietnam records world-highest trade surplus with US, surpassing Mexico, China

articles.author: Brian Wong
articles.description:
Two former leaders of a now-disbanded alliance behind Hong Kong’s annual Tiananmen Square vigil have a case to answer in a high-profile trial after judges ruled the evidence supported prosecutors’ allegations that the activists incited others to overthrow the Communist Party of China leadership.
Three High Court judges on Friday found that the evidence appeared to suggest Lee Cheuk-yan and Chow Hang-tung committed a subversion offence as leaders of the Hong Kong Alliance in Support of Patriotic...
articles.title: 2 anti-China activists have case to answer in subversion trial, court rules

articles.author: Susan Jung
articles.description:
Pink peppercorns look like pepper and are sometimes sold along with white, black and green peppercorns in a mixed packet, but unlike the other three, which are the dried fruit of the Piper nigrum shrub in different stages of ripeness, they are harvested from at least two plants that are unrelated to the pepper family.
Also called poivre rose, the pink peppercorn’s colour, texture (it has a delicate crunch) and flavour – sweet, aromatic and only slightly peppery, without the “hotness” of true...
articles.title: 2 pink peppercorn recipes that bring out their sweet aromatic flavour

articles.author: Mia Nurmamat
articles.description:
Apple announced a reduction in the App Store commissions it charges developers in China ahead of the annual World Consumer Rights Day, drawing approval from the country’s biggest gaming companies Tencent Holdings and NetEase.
The US tech company said it would reduce the commission for standard in-app purchases and paid app transactions on iPhone and iPad to 25 per cent, from the current 30 per cent, according to a statement on its website on Thursday.
Meanwhile, the commission rate for...
articles.title: Apple reduces App Store commissions in China in move applauded by Tencent, NetEase

articles.author: Yeon Woo Lee
articles.description:
Declining fertility rates have long been viewed as a drag on economic growth, but the outlook may not be entirely bleak for Asian economies such as China, South Korea and Japan, analysts said.
Demographic pressure was accelerating investment in robotics and artificial intelligence (AI) in these rapidly ageing yet technologically advanced countries, helping offset labour shortages and sustain productivity even as populations shrank, they argued.
Analysts at Bank of America (BofA) Global Research...
articles.title: China’s AI adoption may limit economic fallout of its rapidly ageing population: analysts

articles.author: Paul McNamara
articles.description:
Wales boss Craig Bellamy said on Thursday he was “very disappointed” that his attempts to convince Tottenham Hotspur defender Ashley Phillips to ditch England for a World Cup push with The Dragons had been made public.
The clearly annoyed Bellamy, in Hong Kong to attend the draw for the HKFC Standard Chartered Soccer Sevens, said making the discussions public “does us no favours”.
It emerged this week that Bellamy was aiming to include 20-year-old Phillips in his squad for a World Cup play-off...
articles.title: Wales boss Craig Bellamy ‘really disappointed’ that Phillips switch talks made public

articles.author: The Star
articles.description:
Businessman Albert Tei has released a photo purportedly showing a Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) officer brandishing a firearm to back his claims that he had a gun pointed at him during a raid on his home last November.
Speaking to reporters at the court complex in Kuala Lumpur on Friday, Tei said the photo was sent to him on Monday via an unknown number.
“I admit, the photo is not very clear but I believe it was taken from an MACC officer’s body camera,” he said. “What is the...
articles.title: Malaysian businessman releases photo of armed officer to prove he was held at gunpoint

articles.author: Vivian Au
articles.description:
Donald Liao Poon-huai, one of Hong Kong’s most influential government architects and public housing visionaries who became the first Chinese official under British rule to serve as secretary for district administration, has died at the age of 96.
His family confirmed his death to the South China Morning Post on Friday, with one member saying he died peacefully on Thursday morning at home, surrounded by family and friends.
Known as a pioneer of Hong Kong’s subsidised Home Ownership Scheme, Liao...
articles.title: Donald Liao, the architect who shaped Hong Kong’s housing landscape, dies at 96

articles.author: Jevans Nyabiage
articles.description:
As conflict in the Middle East pushes oil beyond US$100 per barrel, Angola and other African producers are in line to be among the main beneficiaries.
On Thursday, following renewed tanker attacks, Brent crude oil prices surged back past US$100 a barrel, having reached a peak of US$119.50 on Monday, the highest level since 2022.
The closure of the Strait of Hormuz, a key maritime chokepoint through which about 20 million barrels of oil and petroleum products flow daily, has crippled energy...
articles.title: How Middle East conflict and soaring oil prices will affect Angola’s Chinese debt deals

articles.author: Zoey Zhang
articles.description:
A young girl from central China earned widespread praise online after fearlessly confronting riding instructors over why they assigned her friends vicious horses.
Nine-year-old Langlang from Huangshi in Hubei province has been travelling the world with her parents since she was a baby.
While travelling in Egypt with her parents on March 4, she was taking a riding lesson with two friends at a local equestrian club.
Although the pair were beginners, the coaches assigned them two ill-tempered...
articles.title: China girl goes viral after confronting riding instructors for assigning vicious horses to friends

articles.author: Harvey Kong
articles.description:
Hong Kong authorities have received 221 complaints about illegal petrol stations in the first two months of the year, averaging about 111 per month – 42 per cent higher than the monthly average in 2025 – as drivers continue to grapple with rising fuel prices caused by the US-Israel war with Iran.
The Fire Services Department said on Friday that prosecutions in January and February had risen even more sharply, increasing 85 per cent over last year’s monthly average, with illegal operators...
articles.title: Jump in illegal refuelling complaints as Hong Kong grapples with rising oil prices

articles.author: Enoch Yiu
articles.description:
Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing (HKEX) has unveiled its biggest listing reforms since 2018, broadening its special listing regime for innovative companies and opening the door for smaller and more diverse firms to list in the city, the bourse operator said on Friday.
HKEX proposed lowering the minimum threshold for companies to list under the weighted voting rights (WVR) regime to a minimum valuation of HK$20 billion (US$2.6 billion), half the current requirement of at least HK$40 billion.
It...
articles.title: HKEX opens door for diverse innovative firms to list with biggest reforms since 2018

articles.author: Maria Siow
articles.description:
Australia’s decision to send a surveillance aircraft and air-to-air missiles to the Gulf highlights the difficult position the country now faces: supporting US and regional partners while trying to avoid being drawn deeper into the widening conflict.
Analysts said the government was “walking a very fine line” with the deployment, signalling support for partners under Iranian attacks while stopping short of committing Australia to offensive operations.
At the same time, they said Canberra was...
articles.title: Australia walks ‘very fine line’ with Gulf deployment amid Iran war

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
Nasa cleared its moon rocket on Thursday for an April launch with four astronauts after completing the latest round of repairs.
The 98-metre (322-foot) rocket will roll out of the hangar and back to the pad next week at Florida’s Kennedy Space Centre, leading to a launch attempt as early as April 1. It will mark humanity’s first trip to the moon in more than 50 years.
The timing is interesting. From the end of March, US President Donald Trump is slated to visit China and meet with President Xi...
articles.title: Nasa clears Artemis moon rocket for an April launch with 4 astronauts

articles.author: Connor Mycroft
articles.description:
Greater Bay Airlines will more than double its fuel surcharge on certain routes starting next week, becoming the last Hong Kong passenger carrier to raise prices amid the ongoing conflict in the Middle East.
The airline announced on Friday that it would raise prices due to “surging fuel costs,” with the new surcharges taking effect from March 18.
The charge on the carrier’s flights to Hong Kong from all destinations except mainland China, Taiwan, Japan, the Maldives and the Philippines will rise...
articles.title: Greater Bay Airlines to raise fuel surcharges, joining Hong Kong rivals as costs soar

articles.author: Zhu Wenqian
articles.description:
Chow Tai Fook Jewellery Group’s recent launch of a series of high-priced gold-inlaid accessories on the mainland has sparked online debate amid China’s slowing consumer market.
Last week, the Hong Kong-listed jeweller showcased several items on its official Weibo account, including a diamond-studded gold AirPods case priced at 788,800 yuan (US$115,000) and gold-inlaid hair clips costing 2,080 yuan each, containing 0.42 grams of gold.
The earphone case, made with about 350 grams of gold, was...
articles.title: All that glitters goes viral as Chow Tai Fook unveils US$115,000 gold AirPods case

articles.author: Joyce Yip
articles.description:
In a Chai Wan industrial building in late February, food designer Alison Tan Jia-qi was instructing a room of 20 Hong Kong diners on how to eat rice with a pat of Échiré, an artisanal French butter.
“She perched a sliver of butter on top of the rice. From one of the sachets of soy sauce that came with the convenience store bento boxes … [she] squeezed a single drop.”
Tan’s commands were met with a chuckling crowd, tickled by the stingy amount prescribed.
Tan was reading an excerpt from Asako...
articles.title: Read or eat? Why not both? In Hong Kong, book clubs and events pair dining with reading

articles.author: Coco Feng
articles.description:
Cambricon Technologies, a Chinese semiconductor designer seen as a potential alternative to US giant Nvidia, will pay its maiden dividend after posting its first full-year profit since listing in 2020.
Cambricon, dubbed “little Nvidia”, planned to distribute a cash dividend of 15 yuan (US$2.2) for every 10 shares held, totalling more than 632 million yuan, according to its filing to the Shanghai Stock Exchange on Thursday.
Another 20 million yuan would be allocated for share buy-backs, taking...
articles.title: Cambricon, China’s ‘little Nvidia’, to pay maiden dividend after profitable 2025

articles.author: Reuters,Bloomberg
articles.description:
Asean should position itself as a safe haven for investment amid worsening global volatility, the host country said as the region’s economic ministers kicked off their meeting in Manila on Friday.
“Let us ensure that Asean remains a region where investment is met with certainty and where cooperation creates genuine opportunity for our people,” Philippine Trade Secretary Cristina Roque said in her opening speech.
Energy and financial markets worldwide have been upended with the Iran war in its...
articles.title: Philippines urges Asean to be global investment safe haven as Middle East war rages

articles.author: SCMP
articles.description:
We have selected seven stories from this week’s news across Hong Kong, mainland China, the wider Asia region and beyond that resonated with our readers and shed light on topical issues. If you would like to see more of our reporting, please consider subscribing.
1. Why have China’s arms imports plummeted 72% over the past 5 years?
Beijing’s arms imports have nose-dived by nearly three-quarters over the past five years, as it has replaced overseas weapons purchases with domestic technology,...
articles.title: China’s arms imports plummet, Hong Kong couple’s HK$50,000 Dubai exit: SCMP’s 7 highlights

articles.author: Holly Chik
articles.description:
China has become the first country to mass produce the strongest carbon fibre, which has wide applications for defence industries such as aerospace, drones and robots, state broadcaster CCTV’s military channel reported on Wednesday.
The domestically developed T1200-grade fibre has a tensile strength 10 times greater than ordinary steel, yet it is less than one-tenth of a human hair in diameter, according to the state broadcaster.
Mass production of the ultra-strength fibre at a projected output...
articles.title: China beats US, Japan in carbon-fibre arms race to create world’s first T1200 factory

articles.author: Vincenzo La Torre
articles.description:
Bangkok, Thailand’s vibrant capital city, is now also home to a world-class museum of contemporary art. Late last year, Dib Bangkok opened in a three-storey converted warehouse in Khlong Toei, in an area between Bangkok’s main throughway Rama IV Road and Soi Sukhumvit 40.

Dating back to the 1980s, the original building was redesigned by Kulapat Yantrasast of Why Architecture in collaboration with Thailand-based international architectural design firm Architects 49 (A49).

The exhibition space...
articles.title: Why modern art museum Dib Bangkok is a must-visit destination in Thailand

articles.author: Themis Qi
articles.description:
Tesla has emerged as a rare outlier in China’s slowing electric vehicle (EV) market, posting a massive sales surge in February even as domestic leaders like BYD grapple with double-digit declines.
The US carmaker’s Shanghai Gigafactory delivered nearly 58,600 vehicles to Chinese buyers last month, up 91 per cent compared with the same period last year, according to data from automotive platform Dongchedi.
Sales of Model Y stood at 41,404 units, while Model 3 accounted for 17,195 units. Starting...
articles.title: Tesla’s 91% February sales jump in China defies overall market slowdown

articles.author: Letters
articles.description:
Feel strongly about these letters, or any other aspects of the news? Share your views by emailing us your Letter to the Editor at letters@scmp.com or filling in this Google form. Submissions should not exceed 400 words
The Mandatory Reporting of Child Abuse Ordinance, which came into effect in January, has sparked significant public discussion. However, much of this dialogue is underpinned by a persistent fear: that a child protection report automatically equates to blame or punishment. This...
articles.title: Families need not feel targeted by the child safeguarding process

articles.author: Bloomberg,Agence France-Presse
articles.description:
A video showing Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi looking visibly exhausted after a budget committee session on Thursday went viral online, sparking concerns over her well-being ahead of a trip to the US to meet President Donald Trump.
Takaichi had cold-like symptoms and was advised to rest by doctors, ultimately skipping some meetings with local Middle Eastern ambassadors on Thursday, according to local media.
“Yesterday, the prime minister suspected she had a cold, so she was examined by...
articles.title: In Japan, video of exhausted Takaichi sparks health fears ahead of US trip

articles.author: Ji Siqi
articles.description:
The full implementation of taxation reforms pledged in China’s new five-year plan would substantially ease the fiscal strains on local governments, a leading tax policy expert said, while adding that it would not alter the central government’s dominant role in the country’s fiscal landscape.
As a unitary state, China’s systematic advantage lay in strong central government finance that could coordinate fiscal resources in a unified manner and redistribute them through transfer payments, in...
articles.title: The fiscal family: adviser says China’s tax flows should resemble parental ties

articles.author: Cameron Dueck
articles.description:
We approach from the east, leaving the main islands of Japan behind. The late afternoon sun bounces off the sea in a blinding glare as our anchor chain rattles out of its locker and slides into a small bay off Tairajima Island.
All is still as our sailing boat, the Teng Hoi, gracefully pirouettes in the currents, searching for her point of balance, where she’ll rest for the night.
Below the sinking sun stretch the Goto Islands, or Goto Retto, literally “five-island chain”, an archipelago of 140...
articles.title: Remote villages, surprise cocktail bars and hilltop churches on Nagasaki’s Goto Islands

articles.author: Charmaine Yu
articles.description:
In the densely populated metropolis of Hong Kong, with its relentless pace and vertical architecture, the concept of community can often get lost in it all.
But Hongkongers are always creating new ways to offer a sense of collective belonging while providing much-needed respite from the daily grind. Even seemingly contrasting and irreconcilable activities can somehow be merged into a unique and multipurpose event in Hong Kong.
Here are five things to do this weekend in Hong Kong.
1. Tea Rave

A...
articles.title: 5 of the best things to do in Hong Kong this weekend, March 13-15

articles.author: SCMP Sport
articles.description:
Hong Kong basketball officials say they have not given up hope of getting the city’s teams into the Asian Games, despite organisers cutting the numbers of associations taking part.
The tournament at September’s Games in Japan has been reduced from 16 teams to 12 for the men and kept at 12 for the women.
Regional rankings will be used to determine who plays, and Hong Kong’s men and women are 26th and 21st respectively, leaving them significantly short of qualifying.
But in a statement published...
articles.title: Hong Kong basketball ‘not giving up’ on Asian Games spot, top official says

articles.author: Julian Ryall
articles.description:
They were killed by American bombs. They were held at gunpoint by Japanese guards who fired indiscriminately into the crowded holds and when the ship finally went down, many were left to drown. Eight decades later, the United States is coming back for them.
Hundreds perished when the Japanese “hell ship” Oryoku Maru was sunk in Subic Bay in December 1944. Now, the Pentagon has launched a multi-year mission in waters off the Philippines to retrieve their remains.
As many as 250 Americans are...
articles.title: US returns for WWII dead of Japan’s ‘hell ship’ tomb in the Philippines

articles.author: Cao Li
articles.description:
Hong Kong stocks fell as the US-Iran war shows no signs of ending, with a hardline stance from both sides pushing oil prices up.
The Hang Seng Index fell 0.5 per cent to 25,587 as of 9.40am. The Hang Seng Tech Index dropped 0.4 per cent. On the mainland, the CSI 300 Index was little changed and the Shanghai Composite Index shed 0.4 per cent.
US President Donald Trump said in a social media post on Thursday that stopping Iran from having nuclear weapons and threatening the Middle East was of “far...
articles.title: Hong Kong stocks extend losses as US and Iran dig in heels amid escalating conflict

articles.author: Theodora Yu
articles.description:
Hong Kong’s fresh graduates are facing increasingly challenging career prospects, with 69 per cent of job sectors recording their fewest vacancies in six years, a trend experts attribute to the rise of artificial intelligence (AI) and a sluggish economy.
Figures from the Joint Institution Job Information System, a centralised online job information platform shared by the city’s eight publicly funded universities, also showed that the number of job vacancies fell to a five-year low of 30,798 last...
articles.title: Hong Kong job openings hit 6-year low in 69% of sectors amid AI’s ascent

articles.author: SCMP Style Reporter
articles.description:
Inspired by Gucci’s broad appeal, Demna’s inaugural collection for the Italian brand was a shop window for looks that ranged from the extravagantly formal to the more relaxed and streetwise, all ornamented with statement pieces of jewellery. Here, Puerto Rican supermodel Joan Smalls helps articulate Gucci’s versatility with characteristic poise.








PHOTOGRAPHY PETROS KOUIOURIS
STYLING ARYEH LAPPIN
MAKE-UP BRITTANY WHITFIELD
HAIR CHRISTINA RENDALL
PHOTOGRAPHY ASSISTANTS VASILIOS SMARAGDAS,...
articles.title: Style shoot: Gucci’s first Demna-designed collection riffs on the brand’s diversity

articles.author: Kyodo
articles.description:
The United States has imposed sanctions on two companies and six individuals for their roles in operations that used information technology workers in foreign countries to raise money for North Korea.
The Treasury Department said the schemes, orchestrated by the North Korean government, had systematically defrauded US businesses and generated revenue to fund North Korea’s weapons programmes, including nearly US$800 million in 2024.
The department also accused workers associated with North Korea...
articles.title: US sanctions 2 firms, 6 individuals for funding North Korean weapons

articles.author: He Huifeng
articles.description:
From assisting with office work to providing daily entertainment, arranging blind dates, and even helping with stock market investments, Chinese users are enthusiastically exploring the cutting-edge OpenClaw artificial intelligence tool for various purposes.
While most early adopters are tech professionals, others are jumping in too, driven not only by speculation and the lure of quick gains, but also curiosity and fear of missing out on the latest AI craze.
“Play OpenClaw right, and it can...
articles.title: From stock tips to blind dates: why Chinese are obsessed with ‘raising’ a lobster

articles.author: Nicole Chan
articles.description:
Across Asia’s densest cities, the milestones of adulthood are quietly shifting. Couples share kitchens with parents. Some wait years on public housing lists. Others secure a flat before thinking about a ring. In some cases, keys come before vows. Increasingly, love moves in step with property. Square footage, mortgage approvals and ballot results shape decisions that once felt spontaneous.
At first glance, falling fertility rates might look like a purely economic or demographic...
articles.title: When homes are small and costly, dreams of having a family shrink

articles.author: Reuters
articles.description:
Indian households are rushing to buy electric induction stoves, draining ⁠stocks online and in stores, ⁠amid fears of a potential cooking gas ⁠shortage tied to the Middle East conflict.
India, the world’s second-largest importer of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG), has invoked emergency powers to boost supplies for households even as availability tightens for commercial users including canteens, hostels and restaurants.
Meanwhile, consumers are buying electric cooking appliances as a precaution,...
articles.title: US-Israel war on Iran: Indian homes stockpile electric stoves to beat gas crunch

articles.author: Zoey Zhang
articles.description:
A 102-year-old woman from eastern China has won hearts online with her optimistic attitude and unique lifestyle.
Jin Baoling, a centenarian from a rural area in Taizhou, Zhejiang province, is frequently visited by her son, daughter-in-law and granddaughter.
Known for her longevity and cheerful personality, fellow villagers affectionately call her “Old Baby.”
According to the Taizhou Evening News, Jin is mentally sharp and physically healthy, having not visited a hospital in the past 50...
articles.title: How a 102-year-old ‘baby’ in China hasn’t been in hospital for 50 years

articles.author: Harvey Kong
articles.description:
Conglomerate Swire Pacific has sold part of its stake in Hong Kong flag carrier Cathay Pacific Airways for HK$1.8 billion (US$230 million) to raise working capital.
In a rare move, the group revealed on Friday that it sold 153.05 million shares at HK$11.74 each the previous day. This was a 9.6 per cent discount to the last traded price on Thursday of HK$12.99 per share.
Swire is the latest shareholder to reduce its stake in Cathay, following Air China’s sale in January for HK$1.32...
articles.title: Swire sells part of Cathay Pacific stake for HK$1.8 billion to boost working capital

articles.author: Paul McNamara
articles.description:
Tallulah Wright will take a break from her 15,000-word dissertation on Saturday to try to upgrade the Asian under-23 triathlon silver medal she won last year.
Reaching the end of her international relations degree at The University of Edinburgh, Wright landed in Hong Kong at 6pm on Tuesday.
Forced to scrap plans to layover in Doha by the conflict in the Middle East, Wright, who is “not the biggest fan of long-haul travel”, flew direct from London armed with neck pillow, eye mask, sleeping...
articles.title: Hong Kong triathlon star aiming for Asian glory as dissertation deadline looms

articles.author: Charmaine Yu
articles.description:
This is the 72nd instalment in a biweekly series profiling major Hong Kong pop culture figures of recent decades.
What do Chow Yun-fat, Timothee Chalamet and Doh Kyung-soo have in common? They have all had to keep up with the razor-sharp mind of Hong Kong actress and television host Carol “Dodo” Cheng Yu-ling.
From teaching Hollywood heartthrobs Cantonese to hosting the city’s most prestigious galas, Cheng’s presence is ubiquitous. Anyone who has watched the TVB anniversary awards or the local...
articles.title: How Carol ‘Dodo’ Cheng went from acting with Chow Yun-fat to interviewing Hollywood stars

articles.author: Harvey Kong
articles.description:
Trina Lau spent nearly three months looking for work after she was laid off from an e-commerce firm in Hong Kong in December.
It was the 23-year-old’s first job after graduating with a communications degree last year. The position only lasted for six months.
She sent out more than 50 job applications but only received calls for interviews for six of them.
Lau conceded that it was slow going because the economy was not picking up as quickly as she would have liked.
But now, she said, she had the...
articles.title: ‘I can’t get a job and AI is to blame’: a young person’s lament

articles.author: Xiaofei Xu
articles.description:
BMW could be approaching the end of the tunnel in China as signs of stabilisation raise hopes of a turnaround after the German carmaker reported that sales dropped by double digits in the key market in 2025.
“Transaction prices in the market for our products have stabilised … and are actually improving slightly compared to [the third quarter],” said Walter Mertl, chief financial officer, during a press conference on Thursday.
“If the run rate continues this way, we have the opportunity to go...
articles.title: BMW sees smoother road ahead in China after sales skid in 2025

articles.author: Sam Beltran
articles.description:
Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jnr’s pitch for a United Nations Security Council seat this week was notable for his sidestepping of an issue at the core of Manila’s foreign policy in recent years.
As he appealed to UN members in New York, Marcos framed the Philippines as a bridge connecting developing countries and middle-income economies, without making any direct reference to the South China Sea dispute.
The president’s restrained speech, which avoided mentioning China despite ongoing...
articles.title: Philippines’ bid for UN Security Council seat sidesteps maritime row

articles.author: Xinyi Wu
articles.description:
Some Chinese lawmakers and advisers are pushing to secure higher pensions for elderly farmers, underscoring the persistent income disparity between the country’s urban and rural residents.
The latest government work report, approved on Thursday, confirmed a 20-yuan (US$2.91) monthly increase to basic pension payments for a third consecutive year, bringing the national minimum to 163 yuan. However, some deputies from China’s top legislature contend that this level is inadequate.
“A pension of...
articles.title: China’s rural pensions in focus as lawmakers fight for farmers’ fair share amid income gap

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
California Governor Gavin Newsom said there was no imminent threat to the state, despite a warning from the FBI that Iran could send drones to the west coast in retaliation for war.
Newsom said drone issues “have always been top of mind”.
“We’ve been aware of that information. … It’s all about a posture of preparedness for worst-case scenarios,” the governor said on Wednesday.
The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) recently warned police departments about Iran and a possible California...
articles.title: California’s Governor Newsom says no imminent threat despite warning of Iran drone attack

articles.author: SCMP Editorial
articles.description: The “two sessions” of China’s top legislative and political advisory bodies have concluded with the passage of major resolutions. A number of things set it apart. One is the endorsement by lawmakers of the nation’s 15th five-year plan – a road map with which Hong Kong is aligning its development. The other is that despite the distractions of war in the Middle East between rival power the United States and economic partner Iran, and the roller-coaster impact on the price of oil, China’s...
articles.title: China’s ‘two sessions’ passes smoothly despite global turmoil

articles.author: Charmaine Yu
articles.description:
Whether it is news “straight from the horse’s mouth”, the futility of “leading a horse to water” or the perils of “looking a gift horse in its mouth”, the English language is trotting with equine idioms.
For the South China Morning Post’s resident political cartoonist Harry Harrison, these well-worn phrases provide the perfect stable of inspiration for his latest collection of cheeky illustrations for the Year of the Horse.
This set of eight original watercolour and ink works will be up for...
articles.title: SCMP political cartoonist Harry Harrison’s new Year of the Horse collection to be auctioned

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
An American military refuelling plane went down in Iraq and rescue efforts were under way, US Central Command said on Thursday.
The KC-135 aircraft was part of the operation against Iran but the crash was not due to hostile fire or friendly fire, the military said in a statement.
US Central Command, which oversees the Middle East, said two aircraft were involved and that one landed safely and the other went down in western Iraq. It described the latter as “a loss”.
A US official, who spoke on...
articles.title: US military refuelling plane crashes in Iraq, rescue efforts are under way

articles.author: Enoch Yiu
articles.description:
Arrests in a HK$315 million (US$40 million) insider dealing case underscore Hong Kong’s commitment to upholding the integrity of its stock market amid a surge in new listings and share placements, according to industry players.
The Independent Commission Against Corruption (ICAC) on Thursday said it had arrested eight people after joining forces with the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) earlier this week to raid premises connected to a hedge fund and two securities firms.
The joint...
articles.title: Hong Kong insider-trading arrests send ‘very strong message’ on market integrity

articles.author: Paul McNamara
articles.description:
Darren Read acknowledged he was “a little bit shocked” to be thrust into the breach as interim Lee Man head coach, and downplayed his prospects of landing the permanent role.
Promoted from assistant following the exit of Chu Siu-kei on Sunday, Read made a dream start three days later when he oversaw a League Cup semi-final victory over Tai Po, then relayed news to his audibly thrilled players that their triumph had secured “an extra bonus from the big boss”.
They will meet the winners of next...
articles.title: Hong Kong football boss ‘shocked’ to land job, downplays permanent hopes after dream start

articles.author: Agence France-Presse
articles.description:
Serbia’s president confirmed late on Thursday that his country possesses Chinese supersonic surface-attack cruise missiles, after photos of the weapons attached to Serbian fighter jets leaked online.
Photos, which began circulating on social media and defence blogs earlier this week, showed missiles believed to be Chinese-made CM-400AKG cruise missiles attached to Serbia’s Russian-made MiG-29 planes.
“We have things we do not show,” President Aleksandar Vucic told Serbia’s national broadcaster...
articles.title: Serbian president confirms his country owns Chinese supersonic missiles after photo leak

articles.author: SCMP Editorial
articles.description:
Careless driving without causing damage or injuries is hardly news, except when public figures or people in positions of authority are involved. The incident where Hong Kong legislator Judy Chan Kapui drove against traffic early this year continues to draw public attention as it concerns not just the rule of law but also the conduct of lawmakers under the revamped “all-patriots” governance approach.
So far, the case is being handled in accordance with the law and procedures, and rightly so. As...
articles.title: Judy Chan careless driving case a reminder of high expectations for lawmakers

articles.description: 霍尔木兹海峡是是将石油、天然气和其他货物从波斯湾运往外界的唯一海上通道，具有重要战略意义。伊朗军队目前在波斯湾和霍尔木兹海峡拥有战略优势，有能力威胁航运交通。
articles.title: 伊朗为何要封锁霍尔木兹海峡？

articles.description: 全球经济本已因国际贸易秩序崩溃、乌克兰战争以及特朗普混乱的政策制定而备受冲击，愈演愈烈的伊朗战争成为又一次沉重的打击。亚洲经济体面临的风险尤为严峻。
articles.title: 无人幸免：伊朗战争震动全球经济

articles.description: 中共一直在推动新疆、西藏等地区的少数民族将自己认同为爱国公民。“民族团结法”承载了习近平构建由党打造单一国家认同的使命，被视为保护北京统治，抵御威胁的手段。
articles.title: “民族团结”立法：打造单一国家意识

articles.description: 此次调查矛头指向数十个国家，涉及这些国家对使用强迫劳动生产的商品方面的贸易政策。这是美国贸易代表办公室正在推进的多项调查之一，已引起一些贸易伙伴的不满和担忧。
articles.title: 美国启动贸易调查，矛头指向强迫劳动

articles.description: 北京宣布将把农民基础养老金最低标准每月提高20元。如此微薄的增幅凸显了中国经济的不平等，也引发广泛争议，甚至一些人大代表也呼吁提高农民养老保障。
articles.title: “对农民有点太亏了” 中国农民养老金增幅微薄引发争议

articles.description: 伊朗战争迫使美国转移在亚洲的军事资源，这促使区域盟友重新思考对美国的依赖。分析认为，这场战争将削弱美国的影响力，提升中国信心，并加速中等强国的军备竞赛。
articles.title: 伊朗战争是如何让中国受益的

articles.description: 谷爱凌在旧金山的春节大游行中受到民众追捧，但在美国其他地方，她的身份和行为则更具争议性。她与刘美贤得到的不同待遇也在美国华裔群体中引发讨论。
articles.title: 谷爱凌出席旧金山春节大游行

articles.description: 在对伊朗发动军事打击之前，特朗普淡化了能源市场面临的风险，将其淡化为短期担忧，不应盖过推翻伊朗政权任务的成功。这种误判的严重程度在近日暴露无遗。
articles.title: 特朗普及其顾问对伊朗的严重误判

articles.description: 数据显示，在过去的13天里，有12天未见中国军机在台湾附近飞行。一些分析人士认为，习近平可能在为与特朗普的峰会做铺垫，以显示中国在台海问题上并非挑衅者。
articles.title: 北京悄然减少台湾附近军机飞行

articles.description: 调查发现，对该小学建筑的袭击是美军目标定位错误所致。袭击导致至少175人死亡，其中大多数是儿童。此前特朗普一度声称应对此事负责的是伊朗，而非美国。
articles.title: 调查认定美国应对袭击伊朗小学负责

articles.description: 白宫尚未提供特朗普的议程细节以及中美双方可能达成的协议，这令中国官员感到挫败。美国商界领袖也表示，他们尚不清楚自己是否会被邀请随同总统出行。
articles.title: “习特会”充满不确定性 峰会临近，中国仍不清楚特朗普议程

articles.description: 鉴于中国在全球制造业的主导地位，不含中国元素的无人机很难做到。但乌克兰已把重点放在生产的自给自足上，以在中国供应可能被切断的情况下能够继续制造无人机。
articles.title: 乌克兰成功制造“去中国化”的无人机

articles.description: 特朗普想让伊朗屈服，内塔尼亚胡则想把它彻底打垮。两国一起发动了这场战争，但随着战线拉长，很难看出它们如何能联手结束这场战争。
articles.title: 关于伊朗战争，特朗普和内塔尼亚胡的利益出现分歧

articles.description: 这场战争已在重塑旅行模式、能源依赖格局、贸易航线与战略伙伴关系。它带来的连锁反应可能扰乱美国中期选举、改变乌克兰战场的格局，并迫使中国做出经济战略调整。
articles.title: 伊朗战争如何在一周内改变了世界

articles.description: 华盛顿的拉美政策一直在忽视与危言耸听之间摇摆，中国则保持着耐心和财大气粗的存在。特朗普需要明白，伙伴国家无法单靠威胁来领导。
articles.title: 拉美国家表面附和美国，实际在深化对华关系

articles.description: 沙阿是一名说唱歌手，四年前以独立候选人身份成功当选加德满都市长。本周，他领导的国家自由党在尼泊尔大选中取得压倒性胜利，获得该国现代选举史上最广泛的授权。
articles.title: 他是歌手、是“愤青”，也是尼泊尔总理

articles.description: 燃油是航空公司仅次于人力成本的第二大支出。从历史来看，机票价格会紧跟油价波动。上一次油价因俄罗斯入侵乌克兰而飙升时，机票价格随之大涨28%。
articles.title: 油价飙升，机票价格会随之暴涨吗？

articles.description: 伊朗冲突将如何收场充满不确定性。特朗普在战争初期曾表示，战事可能持续“四到五周”。但此后，总统及其政府成员不断就战争时间表和目标发表前后不一的说法。
articles.title: 伊朗战争何时结束？特朗普说法矛盾

articles.description: 伊朗的最高领袖办公室通常简称为贝特，老哈梅内伊在位期间，贝特的规模从数十人扩大到一个拥有4千名雇员的庞大机构，在国家事务中一直发挥着超乎寻常的作用。
articles.title: 揭秘伊朗最高领袖办公室

articles.description: 官方数据显示，中国今年1月至2月的石油进口量较去年同期增长15.8%。过去一年，中国一直在不断扩充战略石油储备。如今，这些储备预计将派上用场。
articles.title: 中国在伊朗战争爆发前已开始囤积石油

articles.description: 伊朗战争导致石油价格飙升，各国疲于应对。这提醒世人：尽管石油在全球能源需求中的占比已低于往昔，但它在地缘政治与全球经济中仍拥有持久的影响力。
articles.title: “能源武器”卷土重来 石油再次成为地缘政治工具和经济威胁

articles.description: 美国和以色列对伊朗发动袭击后，米勒医生被滞留在卡塔尔。他决定要不惜一切代价离开这个地区，随后经历了一段历时62个小时、耗资近1万美元，游遍四大洲的旅途。
articles.title: 历时62小时、游遍四大洲的回家之路

articles.description: 伊朗表面上是神权国家，但革命卫队构成了这个军事化国家的支柱。分析认为，革命卫队在军事、政治与经济领域的广泛影响力是阻碍伊朗政权更迭乃至任何变革的主要障碍。
articles.title: 伊斯兰革命卫队：伊朗军事化国家支柱

articles.description: 伊朗政权是一个耻辱，应该被推翻。但无休止的空袭把伊朗彻底摧毁，使其变成一个任何人都无法治理的烂摊子。那将是一场无法估量的灾难。
articles.title: 特朗普和内塔尼亚胡应该见好就收

articles.description: 随着原油价格飙升，能源进口严重依赖中东地区的亚洲各国政府被迫采取措施，希望保护消费者免受冲击，同时限制能源使用，以防在这场看不到尽头的冲突中出现能源短缺。
articles.title: 亚洲各国应对伊朗战争带来的经济冲击

articles.description: 伊朗局势带来的连锁反应与一年前特朗普贸易战爆发时的全球恐慌十分相似。经济学家警告动荡即将来临，各国领导人也为其经济后果感到恐慌。但特朗普对此毫不动摇。
articles.title: 伊朗战争给全球经济带来新难题

articles.description: 穆杰塔巴是一名强硬派教士，被视为与伊朗最高军事力量关系密切。美国和以色列曾公开警告伊朗不要让其接班。外界担忧，小哈梅内伊可能会加速研发核武器。
articles.title: 伊朗向美以展现强硬态度

articles.description: 伊朗是中国的盟友和金融合作伙伴，霍尔木兹海峡是中国能源和货物运输的重要通道。近年来，中国对中东的投资增长迅速，若冲突扩大，北京可能将蒙受损失。
articles.title: 中东冲突令中国经济承压 能源、货物运输受阻，投资风险加剧

articles.description: 特朗普的伊朗行动与乌克兰战争有诸多令人不安的相似之处。白宫对伊朗局势的表态多次回响着俄罗斯的辞令，这凸显了一场定义模糊、不设期限的战争所带来的风险。
articles.title: 特朗普的伊朗行动：普京战争的回响

articles.description: 特朗普声称伊朗应对学校袭击事件负责。但最新发布的视频证实，击中学校附近海军基地的是一枚战斧巡航导弹。美军是这场冲突中唯一使用战斧导弹的武装力量。
articles.title: 究竟哪国导弹击中了伊朗小学？

articles.description: 油价比美国和以色列攻击伊朗之前上涨了约50%，人们越来越担心中东战争会对能源供应造成影响。亚洲经济严重依赖从中东进口石油，日韩股市周一早盘大幅下挫。
articles.title: 国际油价突破每桶100美元大关

articles.description: 穆杰塔巴·哈梅内伊长期在其父的办公室协调军事和情报行动。据悉他与势力强大的伊斯兰革命卫队关系密切，但他很少公开露面或发言，个性和政治立场鲜为人知。
articles.title: 哈梅内伊之子继任伊朗新最高领袖

articles.description: 对习近平而言，特朗普肆意动用军事力量印证了他的世界观：美国始终是中国最持久的威胁，中国必须建设一支强大的军队，并确保按照北京设定的条件实现和平。
articles.title: 伊朗战争给习近平的教训 硬实力为王，美国威胁持久存在

articles.description: 娄烨因曾拍摄新冠封控和六四事件等中国禁忌题材而被称为“禁片之王”。他的新作是一部关于摇滚乐队的演唱会电影，这也是他数十年来剧情片创作后首次涉足非虚构领域。
articles.title: “禁片之王”娄烨新作转向演唱会电影

articles.description: 受公务宴请禁酒令、公款饮酒开支缩减，以及年轻一代对烈酒兴趣寥寥的影响，贵州茅台的业绩受到重创。在被誉为“中国酒都”的茅台镇，数百家小型酒厂也受到波及。
articles.title: 茅台崩盘，“中国酒都”的一场宿醉

articles.author: 猫笔刀
articles.description: 文章悼念了中国围棋传奇聂卫平，回顾他在上世纪80年代中日围棋擂台赛中创造的11连胜奇迹，称其在民族自信匮乏的时代成为国民偶像，其成就具有不可复制的历史意义。同时，文章转向对A股市场的分析，指出成交量回归理性、风格轮动持续（资金从大盘蓝筹流向中小盘）、中证500仍是理想投资区间，并简要评论了商业航天、伊朗局势、两融利率、央行降准预期及微信公众号黑名单等热点话题，最终以对时代变迁与人际善意的感慨收尾。
articles.title: 呵，又不打了

articles.author: 猫笔刀
articles.description: 监管层上调融资保证金比例至100%，旨在遏制A股过热行情、防范系统性风险，避免重演2015年杠杆爆仓危机。政策采取‘新老划断’，不影响存量杠杆，市场短期受压后企稳。行情结构严重分化，传统蓝筹股遭资金抛弃，出现大额卖单压制股价，而小盘成长股（‘小登板块’）持续吸金。白银市值突破5万亿超越英伟达，金价稳中有升，地缘政治紧张推升避险情绪。券商板块业绩亮眼却股价低迷，反映市场风格彻底转向成长与投机。投资者被提醒避免‘去强留弱’，建议配置ETF以适应新趋势。
articles.title: 一脚刹车

articles.author: 猫笔刀
articles.description: A股今日成交额达3.65万亿元，创历史新高，市场情绪过热后出现温和调整，商业航天等热门板块回调，资金流向传统行业。两融交易额超4000亿，部分券商融资额度告罄，显示杠杆风险积聚。作者认为此为阶段性洗盘，非行情终结，未来仍有炒作空间。同时，国际局势紧张，美国可能对伊朗发动军事或网络攻击，市场担忧石油供应中断，油价上涨。国内方面，茅台改革渠道模式，推动经销商优胜劣汰；金银价格持续走高，黄金突破4600元/克；苹果与谷歌合作强化Siri AI，全球AI阵营分化明显。整体呈现A股过热回调、地缘风险升温、产业变革与科技竞争并行的复杂格局。
articles.title: 分歧

articles.author: 猫笔刀
articles.description: 本文分析了A股单日成交额突破3.6万亿的极端行情，指出市场由情绪和流动性驱动，而非基本面，属于典型的牛市投机阶段。文章以‘GEO’（生成式引擎优化）概念的突然爆发为例，揭示了资本如何借马斯克言论炒作AI时代的内容优化概念，带动传媒、影视、游戏板块暴涨。作者认为此类概念缺乏实质基础，纯属游资炒作，传统滞涨行业因缺乏共识被资金抛弃。同时提及黄金白银上涨、伊朗局势等外围信息，强调在牛市中应放弃传统投资思维，转向行为心理学视角的博弈策略，核心观点是：当前市场已非投资，而是情绪驱动的投机游戏。
articles.title: 彻底癫了

articles.author: 猫笔刀
articles.description: 本文结合北京物价现象、网络留言管理、马斯克对未来科技与社会的预测，以及A股市场走势展开讨论。作者指出北京餐饮成本高企源于房租与人力，同时批评网络留言乱象，呼吁谨言慎行。马斯克观点被重点提炼，包括AI将超越人类智能、替代信息类岗位与医疗、电力与储能为核心能源、芯片优势缩小、生产力跃升致货币可能失效等，虽被指过于乐观，但仍具启发性。作者认为当前A股牛市情绪稳健，热门板块如商业航天、脑机接口、有色金属受马斯克概念驱动，光伏出口退税取消影响有限。最后强调投资者应适应牛市节奏，警惕情绪泡沫，但不必恐慌调整。
articles.title: 他说学医没前途了

articles.author: 猫笔刀
articles.description: 文章通过链上赌场的投注数据，分析了多个热门事件的概率，包括美联储利率决策、特朗普提名、NBA夺冠、2028年美大选、俄乌停战、世界杯冠军及奥斯卡影片等，揭示市场对政治与体育事件的隐性预期。同时，作者反思了中国演艺圈收入悬殊现象，指出顶级艺人高薪源于中文市场庞大，而普通从业者收入微薄，互联网暴露了阶层差距，导致公众对‘低调炫富’的敏感与反弹。文章强调内容行业‘赢家通吃’的结构性不平等，以及信息透明化带来的社会张力。
articles.title: 什么都敢赌

期货市场中的散户一般都是股票市场上拉过来的，都是有一定炒股经验且风险偏好比较高的老股民，从中可以看出老股民三个特点：

散户老股民的第一个特点，喜欢在期货市场上贸然参与自己不太熟悉的热门品种，这在股市中也非常明显，股市中的题材股炒作，总是起于游资造市，终于散户接盘，也就是说，游资在选择一个题材之前，就需要评估这个题材和标的最终能不能让散户接盘，有两个基本的特点：
 
特点1、题材本身是有一定的媒体热度或基本面，标的具有一定的标签性，让不太研究基本面的散户更容易参与
 
特点2、前期的炒作要有一定的持续性，把图形做漂亮了，才能吸引散户注意
 
这两个特点体现了老股民与新股民的不同：
 
新股民对股票并没有什么判断力，买入主要靠熟人或大V的推荐，主题炒作前期的自媒体造势，主要是吸引新股民的参与；
 
而老股民的特点是基本面会看一点，图形也会看一点，但都不精，所以对那些已经走出漂亮图形，并且基本面有诸多亮点的题材，参与度更高，更容易在主题后半部分的派发中接盘。
 
散户老股民的第二特点是喜欢高抛低吸。
 
这个习惯在一般的品种中赚点小钱，问题不大，可一旦到了供需持续失衡的品种，或者宏观面持续发酵，就很容易成为做大趋势的机构资金或产业资金的对手盘。

这就是，震荡行情辛苦赚小钱，趋势行情做反亏大钱。
 
散户老股民的第三个特点是缺乏投资策略与交易纪律，交易随意性强。
 
散户喜欢抄底与摸顶，随意开仓，参与自己完全不了解的品种，当实际走势与自己的判断不符，证明自己此前的判断有误时，又死不认错，拖延决策甚至持续加仓，成为“死多”或“死空”，结果必然是亏损累累。

这是我24写的一篇分析散户持仓特点的文章，全文见《持仓数据告诉你，散户为什么总是“赚小钱亏大钱”？》

articles.description:
祥昊，让有趣先知楞起来。
查看知乎原文



简单的说，
淬火就是把钢烧到奥氏体状态，这个状态晶格呈面心立方（FCC）结构，缝大，能多溶碳。
奥氏体 200x
然后快速冷却，会变成马氏体状态，由于冷却忒快，来不及把碳挤出去，被迫强行锁在晶格，形成亚稳的扭曲晶格结构。
这就使得本来应该比较规则的结构被碳撑的彻底变形，通过孪晶，位错，过饱和碳原子等共同作用，硬度自然就高了。

至于啥是奥氏体，马氏体，
这就得从金属的凝固开始讲起了。
金属的凝固过程和水结冰非常相似。
都是从液态无序变成固态有序，
也都是到达凝固点后，先在液态中形成一些微小的晶核，然后晶核沿着各个方向长大，最终变成一整块。

不同的是水凝固靠氢键，有明确方向性和饱和性，
你可以理解成乐高积木，只能按固定顺序插，所以雪花只能是六边为基础打底。
而铁凝固靠金属键，没有方向性和饱和性，
你可以理解为只有异性相吸的吸铁石，条件够就能凑上去，
所以受力时原子层可以轻松进行相对滑动，这就会产生韧性，比较抗锤，支持轻微变形。

虽然说金属键不挑食，
但是常压下铁从液态到完全冷却也会经历仨同素异构体，
分别是接近熔点的δ-Fe，这个暂时用不着，甭管。
912°C——1394°C 的γ-Fe，一般讲钢或淬火的时候叫他奥氏体（Austenite），
实际γ-Fe 是基体相，溶碳后的固溶体才是奥氏体，
由于就这一根独苗，一般不会严格细分。
912°C 之下的α-Fe，
淬火整出的马氏体（Martensite）就是碳在α-Fe 中的过饱和固溶体，但结构被撑成体心四方（BCT）。
正常来说，由于碳原子远小于铁原子，抓一把丢进去，就会跟沙子似得卡在铁原子之间，阻止铁原子随意滑动，这就是间隙合金。

当然，加碳是有限量的，如果塞的忒多（≈6.69%），就会变成渗碳体（Fe₃C），成了金属化合物，最终跟陶瓷似得，又硬又脆，彻底失去可塑性。

正常情况下，由于奥氏体是面心立方八面体结构，间隙尺寸大，能塞的碳更多，最大溶解度在 ≈2.11%（1148℃）
而α-Fe 是体心立方结构，间隙又小又碎，碳最大溶解度只有≈ 0.0218%（727℃）。
所以如果单纯等它自然慢慢冷却，就会以含碳量 0.77%为坎（共析点），
碳较少的情况下会先析出铁素体，含碳量低。

然后转变成铁素体 + 渗碳体层片混合的珠光体，成为亚共析钢，
优点是软，好塑型，好焊接，日常用量最大，就是淬火也硬不起多少。

0.77%左右 ，会全部转成珠光体，成为共析钢，
整体不错，均衡，各种工具弹簧用的比较多。

碳多的话，就会优先在奥氏体晶界析出网状二次渗碳体 Fe₃CⅡ，然后剩下的再转成珠光体
成为过共析钢，

过共析钢硬且脆，但是耐磨，必须先球化退火才能用，不然容易碎。
这是正常钢自然冷却的整法，很明显，要么过脆，要么过软，要么过于均衡，
咋地都觉得不得劲。
那既想韧，又想大幅度强化硬度应该咋整呢？
那就得上邪修,
通过快速冷却，使碳来不及析出，强行封冻在晶格里，
变成过饱和的马氏体。
你想想，本来是婴儿穿的晶格现在强行让一米八的壮汉套上，
如果没破裂，那晶格必然会被扭曲变形到极致，
过饱和固溶 + 晶格严重畸变，
使金属正常的位错根本动不了，原子层也滑不动，那不就变硬了嘛。
至于缺点嘛，淬火会产生巨大的应力，
轻微的会使金属翘曲。
中等的变身脆脆鲨，专职弑主。
严重的干脆直接现场开裂，变身魔刀千刃、

所以有时需要重新加热部分回火，来削减这些应力。
由于不同淬火液比热容不同，
就产生了油淬，水淬这两大主流邪修功法。
油萃比热容小，吸热慢，淬火过程中产生的蒸汽膜比较薄，冷却平缓且均匀，产生应力小，
整体比较均匀，不容易翻车，适合高碳钢，
而水淬则会形成厚而稳定蒸汽膜，刚开始冷却慢，等膜破裂后突然暴冷，容易导致冷却不均，产生巨大的应力，不过优点在于淬硬能力很强
一般用于中，低碳钢居多。高碳钢容易直接变脆脆鲨。
所以我国传统刀匠用水淬并不一定是技术多高，可能单纯是过去刀具含碳量不够。
不过我国古代确实有人研究出一些邪修淬火。
比如在《北齐书.綦母怀文传》就有讲，
先用生铁浇在熟铁上，多次熔炼，使得熟铁变成渗碳钢。
然后浴以 5 牲之溺（尿）,淬以 5 牲之脂，出来的宝刀可斩甲过三十札。
是真是假不知道，
不过这刀用的是五牲尿淬 + 油淬确实厉害，
尿中含有无机盐，可以瞬间戳破蒸汽膜，快速冷却，淬硬效果极佳，配合油淬会更为稳定。

气象喵探员，点开我的主页你会发现——这个喵纯纯气象迷，除了气象啥也不会~

嘿嘿，专业的来咯，这题我会。
一朵中等积云的重量可达 500 吨，相当于 300 辆轿车的总重量，但它却能悬浮在数千米的高空中不坠。
这看似很奇怪，但实际是气象学中『浮力平衡』的完美体现，云体会通过热力学设计，使其整体密度持续低于周围空气，从而获得向上的静浮力，而云滴的微观特性确保了水物质在云中的长久停留。

它来了！阿基米德原理是云体悬浮的宏观物理基础
云体悬浮于空中的现象，首先遵循着阿基米德原理在大气中的具体表达。在气象学中我们会通过气块理论来解释这一过程：将云或者其中一部分视为离散的气块，其垂直运动完全取决于气块密度与环境空气密度的相对关系。当气块密度小于环境空气密度时，气块就会获得向上的净浮力，这跟热气球的原理机制其实是一致的，大小可以根据以下公式计算：

其中 g 为重力加速度、V 为气块体积。
这个原理和公式看似好像相当简单，但实则在云里会有相当复杂的体现，云体之所以能够维持比周围空气更低的密度，关键在于水相变过程释放的潜热。当潮湿空气向上抬升并逐渐冷却至露点温度时，水汽开始凝结为微小的云滴，此过程中每克水汽会释放约 2500 焦耳的潜热，这一热量释放极大的改变了气块的热力学轨迹。
与热气球的悬浮原理一致，云内的暖湿气块因水汽凝结释放潜热，密度小于周围空气，遵循阿基米德原理获得向上的浮力，从而支撑整个云体悬浮于高空。
而大气中的温度随高度变化的速率可以用直减率来描述，也就是大家所说的越高的空气温度越低，但这也会把干空气和湿空气做区分处理。具体来说干空气在上升过程中遵循干绝热直减率，约每公里降低 9.8℃；而饱和湿空气则遵循湿绝热直减率；每公里会降低 4~6℃。这种差异主要还是源于水汽凝结潜热的释放，它就像是一个内置的加热器，会显著减缓上升气块的冷却速率。

articles.description:
苏澄宇，自然科学/分享动物们的小秘密/Animalonearth
查看知乎原文




不是的。
刚孵化的比目鱼宝宝和普通鱼类没什么两样，身体对称，两只眼睛分列在头部两侧，在开阔水域过着漂浮的生活 。

但在几周内，就开始“变态发育”（Metamorphosis）[1]了。
其中一只眼睛（根据种类的不同，可能是左眼也可能是右眼）开始向头的顶部移动。
不同种的眼睛位移方式不太一样
这个过程并非瞬间完成，而是缓慢地进行的。延时摄影的观察显示，这只眼睛会慢慢地在尚未完全骨化的柔软头骨上移动，最终穿过或绕过头顶，到达身体的另一侧，与另一只眼睛并列 。
为了给迁移的眼睛让路，眼睛上方的骨骼结构（称为“眶上棒”）的边缘会被身体主动吸收、溶解，从而为眼睛的移动创造出一条通道 。
不同眼位位移类型的颅骨染色图
原本位于“无眼侧”（即将贴近海底的一侧）的额骨，会转移到“有眼侧”（朝上的一侧），并参与构成上方眼睛的新眼窝底部 。
整个面部的骨骼，包括额骨、筛骨（眼前的骨骼）和嘴部的骨骼，都会发生根本性的扭转，以适应新的眼睛布局 。
当眼睛迁移到位后，之前被吸收的骨骼会重新骨化变硬，形成新的“眶间骨”，将两只眼睛分隔开，整个不对称的头骨结构就此定型 。
转变的过程
完成这一系列转变后，比目鱼的身体结构已不再适应在水中漂浮，于是它会沉降到海底，侧卧下来，开始全新的底栖生活 。
开始“躺平” 。
这种生活方式，正是它那张“歪脸”的价值所在。

首先，两只眼睛都朝上，为它提供了绝佳的全景视野，可以在伪装的状态下，无死角地监控上方的猎物和天敌 。如果一只眼睛还留在下面，不仅毫无用处，还容易被沙石磨损 。
为了配合这种海底生活，比目鱼还进化出了一系列“配套设施”。它的身体是左右侧扁的，非常适合平卧。
同时，它不像大多数鱼类那样拥有鱼鳔——这个控制浮力的器官 。没有鱼鳔，意味着它的身体密度比水大，可以毫不费力地待在海底，节省了大量维持身体位置的能量。
当然，最核心的技能还是伪装。比目鱼能将身体埋入沙中，只露出潜望镜般的双眼进行观察 （呆……）。

这种能力并非简单的生理反射，而是与视觉紧密相关。研究发现，如果比目鱼的眼睛受伤或被蒙住，它匹配环境的能力就会大大下降 。
四张照片中的是同一条比目鱼，拍摄时间间隔了几分钟。在最后一张照片中，这条鱼完全把自己埋在了沙子里，只有眼睛露在外面。
这表明，它是在通过“看”来主动调节皮肤色素细胞，甚至有观点认为这是一种依赖“意识”而非纯细胞机制的复杂行为 。

可想而知，比目鱼是一个伏击高手。它通常会选择水流流经的区域，面朝来流方向，静静等待小鱼、虾蟹等猎物被水流“送货上门” 。
如此剧烈的身体改造，背后必然有一套精准的调控系统。科学家发现，这场变态发育的总开关是甲状腺激素（TH）[2]。
蝌蚪变青蛙，也是甲状腺激素 。在比目鱼的变态发育期间，其体内的甲状腺激素水平会急剧飙升，启动一系列基因程序，指挥眼睛迁移、头骨重塑 。
有意思的是，演化似乎真的是能省则省。
它并没有为眼睛迁移“发明”一套全新的基因指令，而是“征用”了一套早已存在的古老基因通路。这条通路（nodal-lefty-pitx2）原本在胚胎时期负责决定心脏、肝脏等内脏器官的左右位置，但在比目鱼的幼年期被再次激活，用于指导头部的“二次装修” 。
真的很方便呢……

问题来了，好吃吗？
好吃。
